solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe miss one meal, shifting tea breaks

indicators.note: breaks says one and the tea word together cut into the shuffled meal
shifting tells us the letters of meal move into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
cha is an old slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet thinks of skipping a meal while tea interrupts the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe miss' defines by example: a miss is a girl, and the answer is a girl's name. 'shifting' turns MEAL into MELA, which ICHA 'breaks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a girl or young woman, and Michaela is one example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Not the women's singles title at Roland Garros?

definitions.text: Not the women's singles title at Roland Garros?

parts.words: Not the women's singles title at Roland Garros?
parts.note: single women in France are mademoiselle, so the married women's form of address is not for singles

explanation.surface: A question about the championship prize at the French Open tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singles title' suggests a tennis trophy, but it is a form of address for unmarried women; Roland Garros is the stadium of the French Open.
explanation.definitionFit: The French courtesy title for a married woman, as opposed to the one used for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Supply long, trailing cape

indicators.note: trailing says the yearning word comes after the headland letter

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A long cape trails behind its wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the cape, but it is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store or stockpile, a noun sense of supply.

clue.text: Maybe gets breeze in prime location for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to prime is to make ready, to set
an area is a location

explanation.surface: A breezy hilltop is a prime spot for climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime location' looks like a single idea, but it is SET then AREA, read upwards to SETAREA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting fresh air pass through something, such as a room or soil, is one example of ventilating it.

clue.text: Two identical switches on top of wall light

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the shuffled letters above the next piece
switches says the letters of two identical swap places into a new order
top of picks the first letter, as the top of a down entry

explanation.surface: A pair of matching light switches mounted high on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' looks like electrical controls, but it signals an anagram; 'light' is a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A light is a pane or window, and this kind has a criss-cross frame of small panes.

clue.text: Secure — in hair-raising fashion?

definitions.meaning: to make fast with a key, as with a door or a prisoner
read literally, with a tress of hair raised high

explanation.surface: Something is fastened in a frightening way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair-raising' usually means frightening, but here it means a lock of hair lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something with a key is the plain phrasal verb; the second sense jokes on a lock of hair raised.

clue.text: Old Turkish sailor, short virile one

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: short says the manly word loses its final letter

parts.note: virile means manly
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old Turkish seaman, short but strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Turkish' looks like a description of the sailor, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a historical name for the Ottoman Turks and their language, so it means of the old Ottoman empire.

clue.text: Enter the champion: a trusted opener

parts.note: to key data is to enter it
the champion is the title holder

explanation.surface: A boxing announcer brings in the champion, a reliable starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests a batsman or first act, but it is someone trusted with keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given keys to premises is relied upon to unlock them, so trusted to open up.

clue.text: Role was out mainly in the garden

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: mainly says the erring word loses its last letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: to be out in a judgement is to have erred

explanation.surface: An actor's role was mostly played outdoors in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was out' suggests absence, but it means was mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ornamental flower bed laid out in a pattern is a type of garden.

clue.text: Nice of Civil Service hosts to hold forth medals

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, 'of' is de

indicators.note: hosts says the abbreviation holds the speaking word within it

parts.note: to hold forth is to orate, speak at length

explanation.surface: A French civil servant hosts a ceremony giving out honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective; 'medals' is a verb meaning gives medals to.
explanation.definitionFit: To medal someone, as a verb, is to honour them with an award, which is to give them a decoration.

clue.text: Timid chap trapping a couple of bees with slipper, worn but posh

indicators.note: trapping says the shy word closes round the a and the bees

parts.note: timid means shy
two letter Bs
a gent is a chap
an eel slips through the fingers, so a slipper

explanation.surface: A shy man tries to catch two bees with his slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' is footwear on the surface but a slippery fish in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes someone keeping up genteel appearances despite poverty, so well-bred yet threadbare.

clue.text: Civic dignitary dressing right

parts.note: mayo, short for mayonnaise, is a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A town official dresses correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests clothing, but it is a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a town council is its chief civic officer.

clue.text: Aces concealed in shirt seams put back

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
concealed in says the letters lie inside the words shirt seams

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Playing cards hidden in the seams of a shirt by a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Aces concealed' as the definition, but 'concealed in' is the hiding indicator; the definition is just 'Aces'. IRTSEAM hidden in sHIRT SEAMs is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are experts, and maestri is the Italian plural for masters of an art, especially music.

clue.text: Creature cayman bit on toe oddly disappeared

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the phrase go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A cayman nibbled a toe and the toe strangely vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly disappeared' removes letters 1, 3, 5 and so on of CAYMAN BIT ON TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amniote is any vertebrate whose embryo grows within an amnion: reptiles, birds and mammals, so a broad term for an animal.

clue.text: Expert putting up tumble drier as ordered

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of tumble drier as are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A skilled worker installs a tumble drier as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' belongs with 'Expert' in the definition, meaning constructing buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A master builder is a skilled builder, an expert at putting up houses and other structures.

clue.text: Old film technique from USSR, heading off endless cash grabs

indicators.note: grabs says the shortened cash word holds the shortened Soviet word
endless says the cash word loses its last letter

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: heading off says the Soviet word loses its first letter

parts.note: the USSR was the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: Soviet film-makers developed a technique and made money.
explanation.walkthrough: MONE (MONEY 'endless') grabs OVIET (SOVIET with 'heading off').
explanation.definitionFit: This was an early sound-on-film system used for newsreels, so a historic cinema technology.

clue.text: Finish on the tiles after Greek jaunt

indicators.note: after says the jaunt word comes behind the Greek letters

parts.note: a jaunt is an outing

explanation.surface: Ending up out partying after a Greek holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the tiles' is a British idiom for out on a wild night, but here it means literal tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling the gaps between tiles with mortar is the final step of tiling a wall.

clue.text: It makes us cross, what short-term personnel go through?

definitions.meaning: a rotating entrance that people pass across a threshold through, turning crosswise
a high turnover of staff, people coming and going quickly

explanation.surface: Something annoys us, like the stream of temporary staff passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests anger, but the door makes people cross a threshold, its leaves forming a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating entrance with vanes in a cross shape, and figuratively the constant turnover of short-stay employees.

clue.text: Issues with hose used by firemen?

definitions.meaning: runs in women's stockings or tights are problems with hosiery
climbing equipment that fire crews carry

explanation.surface: Problems with a fire hose that firemen use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests a fire hose, but it means stockings; ladders is British for runs in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs in stockings are called this in Britain, and the word also means the climbing frames on fire engines.

clue.text: Succulent duck put in stews: ace!

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

indicators.note: stews says the letters of put in are cooked up into a new order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A cook praises duck put into stews as superb and juicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succulent' looks like an adjective describing the duck, but it is a noun for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the prickly pear genus of cacti, which are fleshy water-storing plants.

clue.text: Agent X following stuff on phone

indicators.note: following says the by letters come after the other piece
on phone says the word is heard as spoken over a telephone

parts.note: to stuff is to fill
x is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 2 by 3

explanation.surface: A secret agent X picks up something on a phone tap.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was a British double agent who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Philby was a notorious spy of the Cambridge Five ring, the archetype of a double agent.

clue.text: Feeling happy no more, evidently flipped

parts.note: feeling up means in good spirits
something no more has ended

explanation.surface: Someone's good mood has gone and they have snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' looks like lost one's temper, but it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned upside down: a flipped object has been turned on its end.

clue.text: Promote any number of us, sort of

parts.note: N stands for any number in algebra
our means belonging to us
the suffix -ish means sort of, somewhat

explanation.surface: A request to give several of us a sort of promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promote' suggests a job upgrade, but it means encourage growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote growth in something is to feed or foster it, a synonym in the sense of cherishing.

clue.text: Old people off home to reflect

parts.note: to off someone is slang for killing them, as is to ice them

indicators.note: to reflect says the home word is mirrored, read upwards

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Elderly folk leave home to think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like departing, but it is slang for kill; the Iceni were the ancient British tribe of Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a tribe of ancient Britain in East Anglia, so a people of long ago.

clue.text: I love not being separated

parts.note: love in tennis scoring is nothing, so none

explanation.surface: A declaration that love means never being apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined together as a single unit, as in an all-in-one gadget, is an idiom for united.

clue.text: With warm honey, set about a sort of loaf

parts.note: to warm is to heat

indicators.note: set about says the honey word is placed around the letter a

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, found in crosswords and pharmacy

explanation.surface: A recipe: with warmed honey, start making some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' sounds like begin, but here it means placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from wheat flour with some bran kept in is a kind of brown loaf.

clue.text: Like lubricated gear, maybe, when in neutral

indicators.note: in says the word for when goes inside the colour

parts.note: grey is a neutral colour
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A car's oiled gearbox, perhaps, left in neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neutral' suggests the gear position, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled machinery is smeared with lubricant, so slick and slippery to touch.

clue.text: Solicitor at Law with facility for speaking disreputably

indicators.note: for speaking says the assembled letters are sounded out rather than spelt

parts.note: S for solicitor, at, L for law, then easily for with facility, giving S L EASILY

explanation.surface: A lawyer with a gift for talking behaves shadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility for speaking' looks like eloquence, but 'for speaking' signals that S, L and EASILY sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a sordid, seedy and dishonest manner is behaving without good repute.
